data.current_summary: Model Context Protocol endpoint (JSON-RPC over streamable HTTP)
data.current_description: The same service, spoken as MCP. Three tools need no key — `get_pricing`, `get_docs`, `get_service_status` — and thirteen more mirror the routes in this document one to one; they read your management token from the `Authorization: Bearer` header of the MCP connection, never as a tool argument. There is NO OAuth and no account, and this endpoint never answers 401: a missing or unknown token comes back as a tool-level error that says how to send it. Both protocol eras are served here: the modern 2026-07-28 (no session, `server/discover`, `Mcp-*` headers) and the older `initialize` handshake that Claude Code, Cursor and SDK 1.x still speak. There is no purchase tool: paying is a plain HTTP x402 exchange against a buy URL, because a signed payment must not travel through a model context. GET and DELETE answer 405.
data.summary_suggestion: Model Context Protocol interface for 402cron service
data.description_suggestion: Provides MCP (Model Context Protocol) access to 402cron service via JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP. Three public tools require no authentication: `get_pricing`, `get_docs`, `get_service_status`. Thirteen additional tools mirror REST API routes and require bearer token authentication via the `Authorization: Bearer` header (not as tool arguments). Supports both modern (2026-07-28) and legacy protocol versions. Payment must be handled separately via HTTP x402 exchange, not through MCP. GET and DELETE methods return 405.

data.current_summary: Agent2Agent (A2A 1.0) endpoint — a receptionist that answers every message with the same guide
data.current_description: JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP, A2A 1.0 only: send the header `A2A-Version: 1.0` (without it the request means 0.3 and is answered with error -32009, which says what to send). `SendMessage` returns one agent message with two parts: a text guide and the same guide as JSON (what the service is, live prices from the tariff, buy URLs, docs). This agent keeps no tasks and offers no streaming or push notifications; those methods return the matching A2A errors. It cannot take payment or create tasks: pay over plain HTTP x402 and manage tasks over this REST API or MCP, because a signed payment must not travel through an agent conversation. JSON-RPC errors arrive on HTTP 200. GET, HEAD and DELETE answer 405. The agent card is at /.well-known/agent-card.json.
data.description_suggestion: Provides Agent2Agent (A2A 1.0) interface via JSON-RPC 2.0 over HTTP. Requires `A2A-Version: 1.0` header; omitting it returns error -32009. The `SendMessage` method returns service information including text guide, live pricing, buy URLs, and documentation. This endpoint does not support task management, streaming, push notifications, or payment processing - use REST API or MCP for tasks, and HTTP x402 for payments. JSON-RPC errors return HTTP 200. GET, HEAD, and DELETE methods return 405. Agent card available at /.well-known/agent-card.json.

data.current_description: 5 fields, UTC only, one minute at the finest. Operators: * a-b a,b */n a-b/n. Names: SUN-SAT (day), JAN-DEC (month). Macros: @yearly @annually @monthly @weekly @daily @midnight @hourly. Day-of-week is 0-6 with 0 = Sunday; 7 also means Sunday. Write days as names (MON-FRI). Numbers differ between schedulers: Quartz, AWS EventBridge and Cloudflare number Sunday as 1, we and croniter as 0. Translated for you: "?". "?" as a whole day-of-month or day-of-week field becomes "*". A NUMERIC day-of-week next to "?" is refused, because "?" means the expression was written where Sunday is 1. Refused: Quartz L, Quartz W, Quartz #, six fields (seconds), seven fields (year), @reboot, @every, CRON_TZ= prefixes, time zones of any kind — each with a code saying what to send instead. The response carries the next 3 runs.
data.description_suggestion: Creates a new scheduled delivery task with cron expression, HTTP endpoint, and delivery parameters. Accepts 5 cron fields (minute, hour, day-of-month, month, day-of-week) in UTC only, with standard operators (*, ranges, lists, steps) and macros (@daily, @hourly, etc.). Day-of-week uses 0-6 (0=Sunday); names (MON-FRI) are supported. Unsupported formats (seconds field, time zones, @reboot, Quartz-specific syntax) return 400 with specific error codes. Returns the created task object with the next 3 scheduled run times.

Re-registering a pending URL generates a new secret and challenge; verified URLs remain unchanged unless you add ?rotate=1.
